thesis: Carvana (NYSE: CVNA). Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-10-28) downloaded and read: statements, liquidity and debt notes, MD&A metrics. Q3 revenue 8,040M vs 5,647M (+42%); 9M 21,848M vs 14,719M (+48%); retail units Q3 217,385 vs 155,941 (+39%), 9M 602,103 vs 433,119; Q3 gross profit 1,521M, operating income 714M (8.9% margin) vs 552M; Q3 NI 483M (total, incl. 194M to LLC unit holders) vs 263M. Interest expense fell to 98M from 125M in Q3 after refinancing (Q3 loss on extinguishment 53M on 1.66B notes redeemed with a Term Loan B). TTM (USD millions, FY25 10-K + 9M26 - 9M25): total NI 2352 (1,895+1,401-944), NI attributable to Carvana Co. 1,706; OCF 1330 (1,036+900-606); PP&E capex 217 (147+166-96); FCF 1113; SBC 97. Close 71.78 (2026-11-18) x 1,103,261,100 shares (Class A 722,713,745 + Class B 380,547,355, 10-Q cover 2026-10-26; Class B pairs with exchangeable LLC units, 34.9% held by LLC unit holders, so A+B is used as the economic count; approximation flagged) = 79.2B = 33.7x TTM total NI; FCF yield 1.4%. Debt 5,228M (long term 4,874, current 283, short term revolvers 71) vs cash 3,049M, plus 2,130M tax receivable agreement liability and 896M finance receivables held for sale. Price implies sustained unit growth near 40% with expanding margin; evidence in the filing supports the growth but valuation is rich on cash flow and peers are unread. Stock fell 5.2% on 2026-11-19 (68.01 stockanalysis.com, 67.99 Yahoo, same day, cause not investigated).
counterthesis: Valuation: 34x earnings and a 1.4% FCF yield, with 9M OCF of 900M after a 1,025M inventory build; growth is capital and working capital intensive. Total NI includes tax benefit effects: deferred taxes 157M in the cash flow and a 2,905M deferred tax asset; 9M26 tax rate 10.9% (171/1,572) is below statutory, so earnings may be flattered. Quality of earnings: gains on loan sales 1,084M in 9M (about 26% of gross profit) depend on securitization and loan sale markets, spreads fell in Q3; other expense includes 62M unrealized warrant loss and Root warrant revenue is non-cash. Leverage 5.2B debt, TRA 2.1B owed mostly to related parties (1,645M), related party transactions with DriveTime (VSCs, servicing). Used car price appreciation helped revenue per unit (28,263 vs 25,625). Subprime-type credit exposure, tariffs and consumer credit shocks are not assessed. Peers (CarMax, AutoNation, Lithia, Cars.com), own history and 8-K release unread.
invalidation: Invalidated if retail unit growth falls below about 15% while gross profit per unit stops rising, if loan sale spreads compress further or securitization markets close, if FCF stays under 2% of market cap as inventory grows, or if related party or TRA obligations rise materially.
